chunks: I mentioned to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) our statement regarding the successors — that obedience to them is obligatory. So he said: 'Yes.'
They are the ones about whom God the Exalted said: 'Obey God and obey the Messenger and those in authority from among you' [4:59]
And they are the ones about whom God Mighty and Majestic said: 'But rather, only God is your guardian, and His Messenger, and those who have believed' [5:55]

key_terms.أُولِي الْأَمْرِ: Those in authority — interpreted in Shia tradition as the Imams
key_terms.الأوصياء: The Successors/Legatees — the divinely appointed Imams after the Prophet
key_terms.وَلِيّ: Guardian/Master — in 5:55, understood as referring to the Imam's authority

ai.seo_question: What Quran verses support the obligation of obeying the Imams in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the doctrinal Shia position that obedience to the Imams (al-Awsiya, the divinely appointed successors) is obligatory. He grounds this obligation directly in two Quranic verses: 4:59 (Uli al-Amr) and 5:55 (the wilaya verse), interpreting both as referring specifically to the Imams of Ahl al-Bayt. This hadith comes from the foundational chapter on the necessity of obeying the Imams, and the questioner, al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Ala, was a trusted companion testing and confirming the Imam's authoritative teaching.
